sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the toggle
sections.what: Brings in the sun and moon icons and the theme functions for reading and setting the theme.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are the tools needed to read and change the theme.

sections.name: ThemeToggle
sections.title: Button that flips light and dark
sections.what: Draws a small icon button that switches to the other theme. Its label and hover text name the mode it will switch to, and it reports a pressed state when dark mode is on.
sections.why: Likely reason: the pressed state and labels help users with screen readers understand the control.
sections.watch_out: The icon and label show the mode the click will switch to, not the current mode, which can be misread.

summary: A small button that switches the app between its light house style and its dark style.
purpose: Lets the user change the look of the app with one click.
why: Likely reason: the dark layer is offered as an alternative appearance. The code comment only describes what it switches between.
how: Reads the current theme. Shows a sun icon in dark mode and a moon icon in light mode. Clicking sets the other theme. The label and hover text tell the user which mode the click will switch to.
inputs: An optional class name from the parent, and the current theme from the theme helper.
outputs: Changes the theme through the theme helper. Whether the choice is saved between visits is decided in the theme helper, which is not shown here.
risks: The icon shows the mode the click will switch to, not the mode the user is in, so a user may read the sun icon as the current mode.
debug: If the button does nothing, check the theme helper. If the look does not stick after a reload, check the saving step in the theme helper, not this file. If the button looks wrong, check the class name passed in by the parent.
